entries.name: Ahmad Rahman

expected.sentence:
Convicted under Michigan's felony-murder doctrine for his role in the incident in which Wayne State student Franklin Abramson was killed; sentenced to life without parole though he maintained he did not fire the fatal shot. Sentence commuted by Gov. John Engler in 1992 and released after more than two decades.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — life without parole (commuted 1992)

entries.rationale: Contemporaneous November 25, 1992 wire report says freed Wednesday and quotes him leaving Lakeland. November 25 was Wednesday. Distinguish prior Friday commutation from actual departure. Refines existing November month; preserves documented 21 years and other fields.

entries.name: Alberta Wicker Africa

expected.charges: Charges arising from the May 20, 1977 armed confrontation at the MOVE house and the related federal bomb-conspiracy prosecution
expected.sentence: Seven years; sentenced in August 1981 and released after completing the term in 1988

entries.rationale: Workers Vanguard May 20, 1988 original page 12 visually verified: completed seven years and released May 13 this year. Refines year-only release; does not infer exact admission from the sentence.

entries.name: Al Larcinese

expected.charges: Criminal contempt of a federal restraining order barring picketing.
expected.sentence:
One week in federal prison (December 1977).

Verdict as recorded: Convicted of criminal contempt without a jury and sentenced on December 12, 1977 to one week in federal prison.

Charges as recorded: Criminal contempt of a federal restraining order barring picketing during a week-long wildcat strike (the summer 1977 "heat walkout") at Chrysler's Trenton Engine Plant, as a member of UAW Local 372 — one of seven workers ("the Trenton 7") singled out from hundreds of pickets.

updates.sentence:

entries.rationale: Sixth Circuit opinion 599 F.2d 120 explicitly dates sentencing December 13, 1977. Correct case date and matching sentence text. One-week sentence does not establish actual admission or release. Biography remains unchanged, including its older conflicting sentencing date, outside this case-only scope.
